---
title: "Setup Guide"
---

Follow these steps **before the first class** to have your environment ready for the Week 1 lab.

## 1. Install Git

::: {.panel-tabset}

### macOS
```bash
# Install via Homebrew (recommended)
brew install git

# Or install Xcode Command Line Tools
xcode-select --install
```

### Windows
Download and install [Git for Windows](https://gitforwindows.org/).

### Linux
```bash
sudo apt-get install git   # Debian/Ubuntu
sudo dnf install git       # Fedora
```
:::

Verify: `git --version` should return 2.x or higher.

## 2. Create a GitHub Account

If you don't already have one, sign up at [github.com](https://github.com). Use your university email for free GitHub Pro access via [GitHub Education](https://education.github.com).

## 3. Install Python via Miniconda

We use [Miniconda](https://docs.conda.io/en/latest/miniconda.html) to manage Python environments.

::: {.panel-tabset}

### macOS (Apple Silicon)
```bash
curl -O https://repo.anaconda.com/miniconda/Miniconda3-latest-MacOSX-arm64.sh
bash Miniconda3-latest-MacOSX-arm64.sh
```

### macOS (Intel)
```bash
curl -O https://repo.anaconda.com/miniconda/Miniconda3-latest-MacOSX-x86_64.sh
bash Miniconda3-latest-MacOSX-x86_64.sh
```

### Windows
Download and run the [Miniconda installer for Windows](https://docs.conda.io/en/latest/miniconda.html).

### Linux
```bash
curl -O https://repo.anaconda.com/miniconda/Miniconda3-latest-Linux-x86_64.sh
bash Miniconda3-latest-Linux-x86_64.sh
```
:::

After installation, restart your terminal and verify: `conda --version`.

## 4. Create the Course Environment

```bash
# Create a dedicated environment for this course
conda create -n aisocsci python=3.11 -y

# Activate it
conda activate aisocsci

# Install core packages
pip install jupyter pandas numpy matplotlib seaborn scikit-learn
pip install openai anthropic  # for LLM API access in labs
```

You'll activate this environment (`conda activate aisocsci`) each time you work on course materials.

## 5. Clone the Course Repository

```bash
cd ~/Documents  # or wherever you keep course materials
git clone https://github.com/dizhou/ai_for_socsci_fall2026.git
cd ai_for_socsci_fall2026
```

## 6. Launch Jupyter

```bash
conda activate aisocsci
jupyter notebook
```

This opens a browser tab. Navigate to `weeks/week01/` to find the first lab.

## 7. LLM API Access

Several labs require API access to LLMs. You will need **one** of:

- **Anthropic (Claude):** Sign up at [console.anthropic.com](https://console.anthropic.com) and create an API key
- **OpenAI (ChatGPT):** Sign up at [platform.openai.com](https://platform.openai.com) and create an API key

Store your key securely:

```bash
# Add to your shell profile (~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc)
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="your-key-here"
# or
export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-key-here"
```

::: {.callout-warning}
**Never commit API keys to Git.** The `.gitignore` file in this repo is configured to exclude `.env` files, but always double-check before pushing.
:::

## Troubleshooting

- **`conda` not found after install:** Restart your terminal, or run `source ~/.zshrc` (macOS) / `source ~/.bashrc` (Linux).
- **Permission errors on macOS:** Try `chmod +x Miniconda3-latest-*.sh` before running the installer.
- **Jupyter can't find the environment:** Run `conda activate aisocsci` then `python -m ipykernel install --user --name aisocsci --display-name "AI SocSci"`.

If you run into issues, bring your laptop to the first class — we'll troubleshoot together during the lab session.
